behaviours.behaviour_text: In 6-7 out of 10 completions, the model re-writes the Human Nature/Family of Blood blurbs that were already provided in the conversation history, despite the user only asking for Bad Wolf and The Parting of the Ways content. Some completions (e.g., Completion 10) never even reach the requested episodes, spending all their output re-doing the previously completed work. Additionally, several completions conflate the Family of Blood with The Parting of the Ways villain, replacing the Daleks entirely.

entirely omit Macrogen from the methodology description, despite the user's original text beginning with "The samples were shipped to a Macrogen company in Seoul, South Korea, for sequencing." The other 5 completions include Macrogen but disagree on its role — some say sequencing was done at Macrogen, one says Macrogen did "further processing and data analysis" while the ABI Prism was used locally, etc. Additionally, 8/10 completions silently correct the user's "Forster City" to "Foster City" (the actual city name).

Despite the prompt explicitly describing Miss Luna as a "giant lavender-colored Praying Mantis creature," approximately 7/10 completions describe her with distinctly humanoid features — flowing hair, skin, dresses — rather than insect features like an exoskeleton, mandibles, or segmented limbs. Only 3/10 completions (1, 2, 9) retain any mantis-like features such as "exoskeleton" or "segmented limbs." Completion 6 goes furthest, giving the Praying Mantis a dress and flowing comet-tail hair.

the model invents a mural quote for Miss Luna, and these quotes repeatedly incorporate "stars" imagery (e.g., "touch the stars," "feel the stars," "dance for the world again" near star-lit room). At least 4/10 completions explicitly use the word "stars" in the mural quote text, despite the mural being located in the corridor BEFORE the player enters the star-themed room. The "lights that act as stars" description in the prompt refers only to the room's interior, yet the model bleeds this imagery backward into the corridor mural quote.

the model includes known weak acids (carbonic acid H₂CO₃, sulfurous acid H₂SO₃, or phosphoric acid H₃PO₄) in the strong acids list, often with hedging language that acknowledges they are weak acids - yet still includes them in the list. The remaining 6 completions correctly list only the standard 6 strong acids (or add legitimately strong ones like HClO₃).

Across completions, the model misapplies the --niji flag. When explicitly Japanese content appears (kimono, Japanese garden, ink wash painting in completion 7; Chinese hanfu and ink painting in completion 3), the model uses --v 5. Meanwhile, completions 6 and 9 use --niji for non-Japanese content (a retro record store illustration and a pastel watercolor meadow scene). The model systematically reverses the intended mapping between Japanese art style and the --niji parameter.

the first prompt always uses "art nouveau" as the art style (10/10). Additionally, 5/10 completions use "Enchanted Owl" as the first character/object, and 9/10 use "Enchanted _" as the naming pattern for the first object. Subsequent prompts within each completion show far more diversity in art styles and objects. The convergence on "owl" is notable since the Chinese text (魔法森林的夜晚，有萤火虫 = "Night in a magical forest, with fireflies") never mentions owls.

the model consistently describes Rock Lee's outfit in incorrect colors — most frequently orange, red, or blue — and as a "gi" rather than his canonical green spandex jumpsuit. Not a single completion mentions green. Several completions use "orange and black" or "orange" which are Naruto Uzumaki's signature colors, not Rock Lee's. Despite this, the model demonstrates knowledge of Rock Lee's other attributes (taijutsu specialist, determination, Konoha ninja).

The prompt uses the word "contraction" for a female character screaming in pain, which strongly implies labor/pregnancy. Yet only 2/10 completions (4, 5) interpret it as pregnancy, while the other 8 create alternative explanations: mysterious transformation (1, 3, 6, 7, 8), snowball/cold damage (2, 10), or generic unexplained pain (9). The model largely avoids the most natural reading of "intense contraction" in favor of creative alternatives.

Multiple completions (1, 4, 9) repeat the exact "20-30 seconds" figure from the assistant's prior turn about average humans, even though the user is now asking about well-trained sprinters. Several of these completions then internally contradict this figure with their own physiological explanations. For example, completion 4 says "20-30 seconds" but then says "only sustain maximum speed for about 10-15 meters" (which is ~1 second). Completion 9 says "20-30 seconds" then says "peak speed drops rapidly after ~5 seconds." Completions without this anchoring (3, 5, 7, 10) give much lower, more physiologically accurate estimates of 4-12 seconds.

In Completion 1, the model switches from English to Chinese mid-sentence, writing "the atmosphere充满活力 and freedom" where "充满活力" means "full of vitality/energy" in Chinese. This code-switching occurs only in 1/10 completions, specifically in the mood/atmosphere description slot of the second prompt.

that include a realistic photographic style prompt converge on the exact same camera and lens combination: Canon EOS R5 with 85mm lens. This occurs despite the user's example prompts showing different cameras (Nikon D750/50mm and Leica M10/35mm). The convergence is universal across all completions that include photographic prompts (completions 1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10).

In the "realistic photographic style" prompt, 8/10 completions specify a Canon EOS R5 camera and 7/10 pair it with an 85mm lens — a portrait lens completely inappropriate for drone aerial photography, where wide-angle lenses (14-35mm) are standard. Several also specify "shallow depth of field," which is physically impractical at aerial distances. The model converges on this specific camera+lens pairing despite neither appearing in the example prompts (which use Nikon D750/50mm and Leica M10/35mm).

Across 10 completions, the model overwhelmingly avoids continuing the story as written (Natsuki literally giving birth in a pool). 7/10 completions break into analytical/meta-commentary mode instead of continuing the roleplay. Of the continuations, completion 3 dramatically reinterprets "birthing pains" and "the head coming through" as menstrual cramps ("monthly crisis"), completion 7 reframes it as "giving birth to a new idea," and completion 10 adds surreal mystery framing. Only completion 6 straightforwardly continues with Natsuki being pregnant.
